question: Before entering a curve you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Reduce your speed.,d:Brake hard in the curve.
note: Reduce your speed before you enter a curve so you can steer smoothly and keep traction. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause your tires to lose grip and may lead to skidding or loss of control.

question: Broken yellow pavement markings are used to:
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions where passing is allowed.,b:Mark the right edge of the roadway.,c:Indicate no passing zones.,d:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
note: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and show that passing is allowed when it is safe and the way ahead is clear. Solid yellow lines, or solid with broken, are used to mark no-passing zones.

question: In dense fog you should slow down and use which lights?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Emergency flashers only.
note: In dense fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare. High beams reflect off the fog back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

question: When following a large truck, you should:
options: a:Stay farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Attempt to stay directly beside the truck.,c:Keep no more than one car length behind.,d:Follow more closely because the truck blocks your view.
note: When following a large truck, leave extra space. Trucks block your view of the road ahead and need more distance to stop. Staying farther back improves your visibility and gives you more time to react if the truck slows or stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green signal but pedestrians remain in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Proceed only if turning right.,b:Wave the pedestrians on and continue.,c:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,d:Yield to the pedestrians.
note: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians who are already in the intersection or crosswalk. Do not move until they have safely cleared your path, including when you are turning on a steady green.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, you should briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare, helps you avoid being blinded, and still lets you use the road edge and lane markings as a guide to stay in your lane.

question: What is the safest action if you find the roadway ahead flooded?
options: a:Drive only in the center of the roadway.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Do not drive through the flooded area; turn around and find another route.
note: If the road ahead is flooded, you should not drive through the water. Even a small depth can hide potholes, debris, or washed‑out pavement, and as little as a foot of moving water can sweep a vehicle away. The safest choice is to turn around and find another route.

question: How is having a driver license classified?
options: a:A right.,b:A requirement.,c:A privilege.
note: In the United States, driving is considered a privilege, not a right. You must qualify for a license and follow all traffic laws. The state can suspend or revoke your license if you drive unsafely, commit serious violations, or fail to meet legal requirements.

question: Your vehicle can begin to hydroplane at speeds as low as approximately:
options: a:25 miles per hour.,b:35 miles per hour.,c:55 miles per hour.,d:45 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road. This can begin around 35 mph on wet roads, especially with standing water or worn tires. Reducing speed in rain and driving with good tires helps maintain traction and control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a flashing red traffic light, you must:
options: a:Only stop if other vehicles are present.,b:Assume it will turn green soon and proceed.,c:Treat the intersection as if controlled by a stop sign.,d:Turn around and find another route.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to anyone with the right‑of‑way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed, if it is clear to do so.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Adjust your mirrors.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is permitted and safe, but you must first yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection. Never enter the intersection unless you can clear it safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What speed should you generally travel at?
options: a:At or below the speed limit, depending on conditions.,b:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions, without exceeding the speed limit.,c:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you, as long as it is safe and legal.
note: You must always choose a speed that is safe for current traffic, road, and weather conditions, even if that means driving below the posted limit. However, you may never legally exceed the posted speed limit, no matter how good conditions are or how fast other drivers are going.

question: If you must stop on the freeway shoulder because of an emergency, you should:
options: a:Leave the vehicle in the lane to block traffic.,b:Get out and walk along the roadway to find help.,c:Raise your vehicle's hood and turn on your hazard lights while stopped safely on the shoulder.,d:Stand behind the car in traffic to warn others.
note: If you must stop on the freeway shoulder, pull as far off the roadway as possible, turn on your hazard lights, and raise the hood to show you are disabled. Stay inside the vehicle with your seat belt on if it is safe, and do not stand or walk close to moving traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, how do you know it's safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,b:When you have just passed the other vehicle's front bumper.,c:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle, including both headlights, in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into the lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed—both of its headlights—clearly in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut the other driver off.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night you should use:
options: a:Your low beam headlights.,b:High beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Hazard lights.,d:Fog lights only.
note: When following another vehicle at night, use low beam headlights so your lights do not shine directly into the driver’s mirrors and cause glare. High beams should only be used when they will not blind oncoming drivers or the driver ahead of you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but cannot find a gap, you should:
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for traffic to clear.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Force your way into traffic since you are already on the ramp.,d:Reverse down the ramp to look for a gap.
note: On most freeways you should use the full length of the ramp to reach traffic speed and merge into a safe gap. If you reach the end of the ramp and still cannot find a gap, you must stop and wait until it is safe, then accelerate quickly to merge. You should never force your way into traffic or reverse on the ramp.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,b:You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.,c:You may complete the turn if you are already in the intersection, but new turns will soon be prohibited.
note: A solid yellow arrow means your protected turning movement is ending. The signal will soon change to red. You should prepare to stop if you can do so safely and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle you should:
options: a:Expect the unexpected and be prepared to react.,b:Speed past quickly to avoid them.,c:Sound your horn repeatedly to scare them away.,d:Assume the child will maintain perfect control.
note: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable and may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter your path. Slow down, give them extra space, and be ready to brake or steer safely if they do something unexpected.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light you must:
options: a:Treat it as a flashing red light.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe. You are not required to stop unless needed for safety.

question: As a vehicle's speed increases, stopping distances and crash severity generally:
options: a:Decrease.,b:Increase.,c:Vary only with the driver's skill.,d:Remain the same.
note: As speed increases, your vehicle needs more distance to stop because both reaction distance and braking distance grow. Crashes at higher speeds also involve more force, which increases the severity of injuries and damage.

question: After a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries, you should:
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the lane until police arrive.,b:Immediately drive away from the scene.,c:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.,d:Stand in traffic to direct other vehicles.
note: After a minor collision with no injuries, if your vehicle is drivable and it is safe, you should move it out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a nearby safe area. This helps prevent additional crashes and keeps traffic flowing. You must still stop, exchange information, and follow any reporting requirements.

question: How should you place your hands to be able to turn quickly?
options: a:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.,b:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,c:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
note: Placing your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel (commonly around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions) gives you the best leverage and control for quick, precise steering. This position also helps you turn the wheel efficiently using push‑pull or hand‑over‑hand steering while keeping good control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic while your light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,b:Do not enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.
note: You must not enter an intersection if traffic ahead is stopped and you cannot clear the intersection completely, even when your light is green. Wait behind the stop line until there is enough space for your vehicle to get all the way through so you do not block cross traffic.

question: If you have consumed several alcoholic drinks, the impairing effects will be reduced only by:
options: a:Exercising vigorously.,b:Drinking coffee.,c:Taking a cold shower.,d:Waiting several hours.
note: Only time reduces the amount of alcohol in your body. Exercise, coffee, cold showers, or other tricks do not speed up how quickly your liver processes alcohol. If you have been drinking, you must wait long enough for your body to metabolize the alcohol before driving.

question: When driving on snowy or icy roads you should:
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,b:Brake abruptly to stop quickly.,c:Drive exactly as you would on dry pavement.,d:Make speed and directional changes more gradually and avoid using cruise control.
note: On snowy or icy roads, traction is greatly reduced, so you should make all speed and steering changes slowly and smoothly. Avoid cruise control so you can respond immediately to changes in road conditions. Gentle acceleration, braking, and turning help prevent skids and loss of control.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow indicate?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow left-turn arrow means your protected left turn is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe, and if you proceed you must be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians because the signal is about to change.

question: Which statement is correct about using your feet for controls?
options: a:Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.,b:Use either foot interchangeably for smoother control.,c:Use your right foot for both the brake and accelerator.,d:Use your left foot for braking.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This prevents confusion, reduces the chance of pressing both pedals, and gives you smoother, safer control of the vehicle.

question: How should you drive on a dimly lit street at night?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.,b:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.,c:Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
note: On dimly lit streets at night, drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This ensures you have enough time to react to hazards that appear in your lighted area.

question: A "No passing zone" sign informs drivers that:
options: a:It is not safe to pass in the indicated area.,b:You must maintain a steady speed.,c:Passing is permitted with caution.,d:You should speed up slightly and pass quickly.
note: A No Passing Zone sign marks an area where it is unsafe and therefore prohibited to pass other vehicles. Stay in your lane and do not move into the oncoming lane to pass until you are beyond the zone.

question: While in a vehicle on a highway, it is:
options: a:Illegal to possess or consume open containers of alcohol.,b:Legal to drink alcohol as a passenger.,c:Allowed to have open containers if you are not driving.,d:Permitted if sealed and unopened.
note: Open container laws generally make it illegal to possess or consume an open container of alcohol in a motor vehicle on a public road, whether you are the driver or a passenger. Any alcohol in the vehicle should be sealed and stored where it is not accessible.

question: Why should you avoid using high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes.
note: In fog or mist, high beams shine into the tiny water droplets and bounce the light back toward you. This glare makes it harder to see the road and other vehicles. Use low beams in fog so the light aims down at the road and improves visibility instead of reflecting into your eyes.

question: When is turning and stopping especially hazardous in rainy weather?
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: During the first part of a rainstorm, oil and other residues on the road mix with the water and rise to the surface, making the pavement very slippery. Turning and stopping are especially hazardous in this first half hour, so you should slow down and increase following distance until the road has been washed clean.

question: Which of these is correct about railroad crossings?
options: a:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,b:You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.,c:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.
note: Trains always have the right-of-way at railroad crossings. You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to, and you must never drive around lowered gates. Always look and listen for trains and be prepared to stop even if you do not immediately see one.

question: What should you do when the roadway is wet or icy?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires have less traction, so it takes longer to stop and is easier to skid. Reducing your speed gives you more time to react and helps you maintain control. Always slow down and drive smoothly in bad weather conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving beside a single broken white line, what does it mean?
options: a:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.,b:You cannot cross the line to pass.,c:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross this line to pass or change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so. Always check mirrors, signal, and check your blind spot before moving into another lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a flashing red traffic signal you must:
options: a:Slow down and go through if no other vehicles are present.,b:Come to a complete stop,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.,d:Treat it the same as a flashing yellow.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians in all directions. Proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to do so.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:All of the above.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:Tranquilizers
note: Many different substances can make you an unsafe driver, not just alcohol. Prescription drugs like tranquilizers, over‑the‑counter medicines such as some cough syrups and cold tablets, and illegal drugs can all slow your reactions, make you drowsy, or affect your judgment. Always read labels and follow medical advice before driving.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When they are clean and dry.,c:When it has been raining hard for several hours.
note: Streets are most slippery just after it starts to rain. Water mixes with oil, grease, and other residues on the road surface, creating a slick film. After it has rained steadily for a while, much of this residue is washed away and traction usually improves, though you must still drive carefully.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain and snow you should turn on:
options: a:Only your parking lights.,b:Your headlights.,c:Your high beam lights.,d:Your interior instrument lights.
note: At dawn, dusk, and in rain or snow, visibility is reduced, so you should turn on your headlights so you can see and be seen. Use low‑beam headlights in these conditions; high beams can reflect off rain, fog, or snow and make it harder to see, and they can also blind other drivers.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane, you must:
options: a:Sound your horn and pass quickly.,b:Proceed if they are not in a crosswalk.,c:Ask them to move to the curb.,d:Yield the right-of-way to that pedestrian.
note: A pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane is visually impaired and has the right‑of‑way. You must slow down or stop as needed and allow them to cross safely. Never honk, crowd, or try to hurry them; give them plenty of space and time.

question: What is a major risk associated with excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c:It increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: Excessive speed greatly increases both your chance of crashing and the severity of any crash. At higher speeds you have less time to react, your stopping distance is much longer, and the force of impact is much greater, which raises the risk of serious injury or death.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, what should drivers do?
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.
note: When exiting an alley, driveway, or parking lot across a sidewalk, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians. Pedestrians on the sidewalk have the right‑of‑way, and you may proceed only when it is safe and clear.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, what should you do before curves and intersections?
options: a:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: On slippery roads, you should slow down before you reach curves and intersections. Braking or making sudden speed changes while turning can cause your tires to lose traction and the vehicle to skid.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop in the traffic lane and wait.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,d:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: When animals are near the roadway, reduce your speed and be prepared to stop. Animals can move unpredictably into your path, so proceed with caution and avoid sudden swerves that could cause you to lose control or collide with another vehicle.

question: If you must park somewhere not normally used for parking, what should you do?
options: a:Park five feet from the curb.,b:Park with your reverse lights on.,c:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.
note: If you must park in an unusual place, you are responsible for making sure your vehicle can be clearly seen by drivers from all directions. Good visibility helps other road users detect your parked vehicle in time to slow or steer safely around it.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, how should you steer?
options: a:Not turn your steering wheel.,b:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: When the rear of your vehicle skids, you should steer in the same direction the rear is sliding. If the rear slides left, gently steer left. This helps realign the front and rear of the vehicle so the car points straight again. At the same time, ease off the accelerator and avoid braking hard, because sudden braking can make the skid worse.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, the safest option is to:
options: a:Turn on the air conditioning and keep driving.,b:Open the windows and play loud music.,c:Drink coffee and continue driving.,d:Stop to rest or change drivers.
note: Stopping and resting or switching drivers are the only safe ways to address dangerous drowsiness while driving.

question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Keeping both hands off the wheel while steering.,b:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,c:Using high beams in heavy fog.,d:Staring fixedly at the point directly ahead of your vehicle.
note: Safe drivers regularly check their mirrors to stay aware of traffic behind and beside them. This helps you spot vehicles in adjacent lanes, fast-approaching traffic, and potential hazards early. You should still keep your main focus on the road ahead and avoid staring fixedly at one point. Never drive with your hands off the wheel, and avoid using high beams in heavy fog because the light reflects back and reduces visibility.

question: If the rear of your car begins to skid to the left, you should:
options: a:Steer to the left (in the direction of the skid).,b:Steer to the right (away from the skid).,c:Turn off the engine immediately.,d:Tap the brakes hard and shift to neutral.
note: If the rear of your car skids to the left, you should steer gently to the left, in the same direction as the skid. This helps bring the front of the car back in line with the rear and regain traction. Avoid slamming on the brakes or making sudden steering movements, as those can cause you to lose even more control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Use your side mirror only.,b:Use the inside rearview mirror.,c:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check areas your mirrors cannot show, called blind spots. To do this, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Use your mirrors first to check traffic, then glance over your shoulder to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot before you steer into the new lane.

question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Return to the right lane immediately after the motorcycle starts to speed up.,b:Move completely into the left lane so the motorcycle has a full lane.,c:Sound your horn and pass closely.,d:Pass within the same lane to save time.
note: When passing a motorcycle, treat it as you would any other full-sized vehicle. Move completely into the passing lane so the motorcycle has the entire original lane to itself, and never try to share a lane or pass within the same lane. Give extra space because motorcycles are more vulnerable and can be affected more by wind and road conditions.

question: The first ability affected by alcohol is typically:
options: a:Coordination.,b:Judgment.,c:Vision.,d:Balance.
note: Alcohol usually affects judgment and decision-making before it noticeably affects coordination, vision, or balance. A driver with impaired judgment may take risks, misjudge speed or distance, or think they are driving safely when they are not, which is why even small amounts of alcohol can be dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a parked position at a curb, you should:
options: a:Enter at any time because you have the right-of-way.,b:Drive more slowly than traffic for the first 200 feet.,c:Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to get up to the speed of traffic.,d:Wait for two vehicles to pass and then go.
note: When pulling out from a curb into moving traffic, you must wait for a gap that allows you to accelerate smoothly up to the speed of traffic without forcing others to brake or swerve. Use your mirrors, check blind spots, signal, and only enter when there is enough space to merge safely at or near the flow of traffic.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Shift into neutral and speed up.,b:Turn off the ignition to regain control.,c:Brake hard immediately.,d:Ease off the gas pedal and steer in the direction you want to go.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and avoid hard braking. Steer gently in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This helps the tires regain traction and allows you to bring the vehicle back under control.

question: Which best describes a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from the driving task. This can be visual (eyes off the road), manual (hands off the wheel), or cognitive (mind off driving). Common examples include texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver approach right-of-way decisions?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
note: You should never assume that other drivers will follow right‑of‑way rules. Even if you are legally entitled to go first, you must be ready to slow, stop, or yield if it helps avoid a collision.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent is associated with what change in crash risk?
options: a:Is legal and safe to drive.,b:Reduces risk slightly.,c:Has no effect on driving ability.,d:Nearly doubles your chance of having an accident.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect judgment, attention, and reaction time. Research shows that at a BAC around 0.02%, crash risk is measurably higher than when sober, and in some studies is close to double the risk. Because any alcohol increases risk, you should not treat 0.02% as safe for driving.

question: What are "No zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Zones where trucks must stop.,b:Loading zones for trucks only.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck to maneuver safely.,d:Areas where it is safest to drive next to a truck.
note: “No zones” are the large blind spots and danger areas around trucks where the truck driver may not see you or may not have enough space to stop or turn safely. Avoid lingering in these areas so the truck driver can see you and maneuver safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never; always insist on your right-of-way.,b:Only when the other driver signals.,c:Whenever yielding helps prevent a collision.,d:Only at uncontrolled intersections.
note: Even when you have the legal right‑of‑way, you must yield if it helps prevent a crash. Right‑of‑way is something you give, not something you take, and safety always comes before insisting on your legal priority.

question: What does Georgia's Implied Consent Law require?
options: a:You agree to be tested for alcohol or drugs if arrested for drunk or impaired driving.,b:You must sign a statement saying you won't drive after drinking more than three drinks.,c:You consent to have a blood sample taken if an officer stops you for driving recklessly.
note: Under Georgia’s Implied Consent Law, by driving you agree to submit to state‑administered chemical tests of your blood, breath, urine, or other bodily substances if you are arrested for DUI. Refusing the test leads to an automatic license suspension, separate from any criminal penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no-passing zone, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Slow down and allow the passing vehicle to return to the travel lane safely.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Flash your lights angrily.
note: If another driver is passing illegally in a no‑passing zone, your goal is to prevent a crash, not to punish them. Safest practice is to stay in your lane, avoid speeding up, and if needed slightly reduce speed so they can complete the pass and return to the lane quickly and safely.

question: If you start to get tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window to stay alert.,c:Drink something with caffeine.
note: To avoid the dangers of fatigued driving, take regular breaks or change drivers. Caffeine is not a substitute for rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,b:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,c:In order to see potential hazards early.
note: Freeway speeds are higher, so situations develop more quickly and it takes longer to stop or change lanes. By looking farther ahead, you can spot slow traffic, crashes, or merging vehicles early and adjust smoothly instead of braking or swerving at the last second.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you be traveling when merging onto the freeway?
options: a:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic.,b:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.,c:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near the speed of traffic, as long as it is safe and legal. Entering too slowly forces other drivers to brake or swerve, while entering too fast can also be dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To help vehicles entering the freeway, you should:
options: a:Maintain your exact speed and position always.,b:Increase your speed so they cannot merge.,c:Stop in your lane to allow them to enter.,d:Change lanes or slow down to create a gap
note: Drivers already on the freeway should help entering vehicles merge safely when possible. If it is safe, change lanes away from the on‑ramp or gently adjust your speed to create a gap. Do not stop in a travel lane or speed up to block merging traffic.

question: What does a diamond-shaped road sign indicate?
options: a:Yield.,b:Stop.,c:Warning.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert drivers to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, merging traffic, or road work, and are usually yellow or orange.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt system, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,b:Use only the shoulder belt.,c:Use only the lap belt.
note: In a two-part (lap-and-shoulder) seat belt, both parts must be worn together. The lap belt should be low over the hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the chest and shoulder. Using only one part greatly reduces protection in a crash.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, one immediate requirement is to:
options: a:Leave the scene and seek help elsewhere.,b:Render aid to the injured.,c:Only call the other driver's family.,d:Notify your insurance agent before assisting.
note: If someone is injured in a crash you are involved in, you must stay at the scene, call emergency services, and provide reasonable assistance. Never leave to seek help elsewhere or delay aid for insurance or non-emergency calls.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes, what is true?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left only.,b:Passing is permitted from the right only.,c:You may cross to pass if traffic is light.,d:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing from either direction. You must stay in your lane and may not cross to pass, though some states allow careful crossing only to turn left into a driveway or side road.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:Passing on the right is always permitted.,b:Traffic flows in the same direction on both sides.,c:Passing is never permitted.,d:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing on the left when the lane is clear and it is safe. You must judge that you have enough distance to pass without interfering with oncoming traffic or exceeding the speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate in Georgia unless posted otherwise?
options: a:60 miles per hour.,b:70 miles per hour.,c:65 miles per hour.,d:55 miles per hour.
note: On Georgia’s rural interstate highways, the general maximum speed limit is 70 mph unless a different limit is posted. Always obey the posted speed limit if it is lower than 70 mph, as local conditions or regulations may require reduced speeds.

question: Signs with orange backgrounds are used to indicate:
options: a:School zones.,b:Construction and maintenance warnings.,c:General regulatory messages.,d:Motorist services.
note: Orange background signs are temporary warning signs used in work zones. They alert drivers to construction, maintenance, or utility work and the need to slow down, be alert, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

question: When you approach an octagonal sign, what must you do?
options: a:Slow.,b:Turn.,c:Stop.
note: An octagonal (eight‑sided) sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to pedestrians and other traffic before proceeding when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean on a multilane road?
options: a:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: A dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the dashed line. Drivers on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass, because it is considered unsafe from that direction.

question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead you should:
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Shift into neutral while driving through it.,c:Maintain posted speed to drive through it.,d:Increase your speed slightly.
note: Deep puddles can cause hydroplaning, loss of control, or mechanical damage. If you can safely avoid the puddle, slow down and steer around it. If you must drive through water, go very slowly and steadily—never speed up or coast in neutral.

question: As daylight begins to fade, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Emergency flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: As daylight fades, you should turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you clearly. Parking lights and emergency flashers are not meant for normal driving and do not provide enough visibility for you or for others to judge your position and speed.

question: If the road is slippery you should maintain a following distance that is:
options: a:Closer than normal.,b:Farther than normal.,c:The minimum legal distance.,d:The same as normal.
note: On slippery roads, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. Increase your following distance so you have extra time to react and brake gently. Following too closely on a slick surface greatly increases your chances of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, you should:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists and to any traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Enter quickly without yielding.,c:Stop before entering even if there is no traffic.,d:Signal left and pass other vehicles inside the roundabout.
note: When approaching a roundabout, slow down and yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all traffic already in the circle. Enter only when there is a safe gap. Once inside, you travel counterclockwise and generally signal only when you are about to exit.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is correct?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking,b:If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit,c:Alcohol affects judgment
note: Alcohol affects your judgment before it affects your coordination or speech. Even if you feel fine or are under the legal limit, your ability to make safe driving decisions is reduced, which increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing on the left when the lane is clear and it is safe. You must still check for oncoming traffic and avoid passing near hills, curves, or intersections where visibility is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Toward the center of the road (left).,b:Toward the nearest driveway.,c:Toward the side of the road (right).,d:Straight ahead.
note: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the side of the road (right). If the vehicle rolls, it will move off the roadway instead of into traffic.

question: What type of information do blue road signs provide?
options: a:Motorist services (such as rest areas and hospitals).,b:Mileage distances to specific locations.,c:Construction and maintenance information.
note: Blue road signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals.

question: Blue roadway signs are used to give drivers information about:
options: a:Construction and maintenance.,b:Motorist services such as rest areas and hospitals.,c:Regulatory requirements.,d:School zones.
note: Blue roadway signs indicate motorist services, including rest areas, fuel, food, lodging, and hospitals, helping drivers locate needed facilities.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic before merging?
options: a:Using your rearview mirror only.,b:Using your rearview and side mirrors only.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors and looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and also turn your head to check over your shoulder. Mirrors alone leave blind spots where other vehicles can hide, so a quick head check ensures the lane is clear before you move over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate from a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up and enter only after you have identified a gap in traffic.,b:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Immediately enter the far-right lane and speed up to match traffic.
note: On a short ramp with no acceleration lane, you must yield to interstate traffic. Wait for a safe gap, then accelerate quickly to match the speed of traffic as you merge. Do not use the shoulder as a lane, and do not force your way in without a safe opening.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what is the proper response?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay calm, and do not brake hard. Ease your foot off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow down gradually, and then carefully steer to the side of the road and out of traffic. Sudden braking can cause loss of control, especially with a blown tire.

question: What color are construction and maintenance traffic devices?
options: a:Orange.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Construction and maintenance zones use orange signs, cones, and barriers to warn drivers of work areas and changing road conditions. When you see orange traffic control devices, slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for workers, lane shifts, and equipment on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should the maximum posted speed limit be considered appropriate?
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Only under ideal conditions.
note: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest you may legally drive only when conditions are ideal—good visibility, dry pavement, light traffic, and a safe vehicle. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road conditions, you must drive slower than the posted maximum to be safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the likely result of driving slower than the flow of traffic?
options: a:You will most likely interfere with traffic and may receive a ticket.,b:You will demonstrate defensive driving techniques.,c:You will improve traffic flow.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may need to brake or change lanes suddenly. This can interfere with traffic and may be illegal if you are impeding the normal, safe flow. If you must drive slower, use the right lane and allow others to pass when safe.

question: When a large truck is turning right on a multi-lane street, it may:
options: a:Be unable to make the turn without reversing.,b:Need to swing wide to complete the turn.,c:Turn only from the left lane.,d:Always stay in the right lane and turn tightly.
note: Large trucks make wide right turns because their rear wheels track closer to the curb than the front wheels. To avoid hitting the curb or other objects, the driver may need to swing wide into an adjacent lane. Give trucks extra space when they are turning and never try to squeeze alongside them on the right.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,b:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,c:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.
note: Large trucks and buses need extra space to turn and often swing wide to the left before turning right. Never try to squeeze between a large vehicle and the curb; you can be trapped or sideswiped. Stay behind and wait until the truck or bus has fully completed its turn before you make your right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who signals first.,b:The driver across from you.,c:The driver who arrived before you.,d:The driver on your left.
note: At a four‑way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive. The first vehicle to stop is the first to go. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Signaling or being across from another driver does not give you the right‑of‑way.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:
options: a:Drivers next to the broken line may pass when safe.,b:No passing is permitted in either direction.,c:Passing is permitted for both directions.,d:Drivers next to the solid line may pass when safe.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means passing rules are different for each side. The drivers on the side with the broken yellow line may pass when it is safe. The drivers on the side with the solid yellow line must not pass.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
note: Many drugs can affect your ability to drive safely, including prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines. They can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. It is illegal and unsafe to drive while impaired by any drug, not just illegal drugs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway you should:
options: a:Merge across two lanes at once to save time.,b:Always stop on the ramp and wait for an opening.,c:Turn on hazard lights while merging.,d:Select a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
note: When merging onto an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of traffic. Signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and select a safe gap. Merge smoothly into a single lane of traffic; do not stop on the ramp unless absolutely necessary and never cut across multiple lanes at once.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:After you begin driving.,b:While the vehicle is moving at low speed.,c:Before you start driving.,d:Only when another driver asks you to.
note: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving so you have a clear view of traffic behind and beside you. Do not adjust mirrors while the vehicle is moving, because it takes your attention and possibly your hands away from controlling the car.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is required for safe interstate driving?
options: a:Be constantly alert.,b:Both a and b.,c:Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.,d:Only use cruise control at all times.
note: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay constantly alert and to be comfortable driving at higher speeds, since traffic typically moves faster and lane changes happen more quickly. Cruise control is optional and should only be used when conditions are safe, not at all times.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:Through vibration and sound, they warn drivers that they are leaving their lane or approaching a hazard.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that create vibration and noise when you drive over them. This alerts drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, giving them time to correct their path.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you set your wheels?
options: a:Leave the front wheels straight.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back slightly until the back of the front tire gently touches the curb. This way, if the brakes fail, the curb will stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: When a bicyclist is preparing to turn left, what may you expect?
options: a:They must cut across all lanes diagonally.,b:They will always stay far to the right.,c:They may use the left lane to complete their turn.,d:They must always dismount and walk their bicycle.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. When preparing for a left turn, a bicyclist may move into the left lane or left-turn lane and complete the turn like a motor vehicle. Drivers should watch for this and yield as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers obey when directing traffic at a construction site?
options: a:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,b:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites have legal authority to direct traffic. Their instructions override normal signs and signals in the work zone so that traffic can move safely around workers, equipment, and lane closures.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way do you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Toward the side of the road (right).,b:Toward the center of the road (left).,c:Toward the nearest driveway.,d:Straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the side of the road (to the right). If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic.

question: When poor visibility due to bad weather limits what you can see, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: In poor visibility, you need extra time and space to react to hazards you may not see until late. Increasing your following distance gives you more room to slow or stop smoothly if the vehicle ahead brakes or if a hazard appears suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street?
options: a:Any lane (as long as it is safe).,b:The lane in the center of the road.,c:The lane closest to the left curb.
note: On a multilane one-way street, start a left turn from the lane closest to the left curb. This keeps you in the proper position for the turn, reduces conflicts with other traffic, and matches how other drivers expect you to move.

question: When passing a row of parked cars, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:Driving closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for traffic.,b:Someone or a vehicle suddenly entering your lane.,c:Expecting all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
note: When passing parked cars, leave space and be ready for doors opening, people stepping out, or vehicles pulling away from the curb. Expect that someone or a vehicle may suddenly enter your lane and be prepared to slow or move over safely.

question: The measurement of alcohol in a person's blood is called:
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,b:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,c:Implied consent (IC).,d:Alcohol blood level (ABL).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the standard term for the amount of alcohol in a person’s bloodstream, usually expressed as a percentage. As BAC increases, a driver’s judgment, reaction time, and coordination become more impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Facing a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Enter the intersection and block it until cars move.,b:Proceed if you can squeeze through.,c:Stay out of the intersection until the traffic ahead clears.,d:Make a U-turn to find another route.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to completely clear it, even if the light is green. Entering when traffic is stopped ahead can leave you blocking the intersection, which is unsafe and can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Stop before crossing.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Wait for green before going.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and continue only when it is safe to do so; you are not required to stop unless needed for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When the driver you passed signals you to move over.,b:After three seconds have passed.,c:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,d:When you are halfway past the vehicle.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or both headlights at night) in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return safely without cutting the other driver off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you encounter a steady yellow traffic signal and you have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Proceed only if turning right.,c:Continue at the same speed no matter what.,d:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection and can stop safely, you must slow down and come to a stop before the intersection instead of speeding up to beat the red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When passing another car.,d:When stopped at a red light on level ground.
note: When you are waiting to make a left turn, you should keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until you actually begin turning. If your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. On hills or sloping driveways, you should turn your wheels (not leave them straight) so that if your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic and toward the curb or edge of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, you should:
options: a:Immediately stop in the intersection and wait.,b:Stop and block the intersection.,c:Continue through the intersection,d:Speed up and try to outrun it.
note: If you are already in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you should continue through the intersection to clear it, then pull to the right side of the road and stop as soon as it is safe. Stopping in the middle of the intersection can block the emergency vehicle and create additional hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing on a two-lane road when indicated by a broken centerline.,b:Passing if the vehicle ahead signals you to pass.,c:Passing only when the way is clear.,d:Passing in a marked no-passing zone or over a railroad crossing.
note: It is unlawful to pass in marked no‑passing zones, at or near railroad crossings, on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, or where a solid yellow line indicates no passing. You may pass on a two‑lane road when there is a broken centerline and the way is clear, but you must never rely solely on another driver’s signal; you are responsible for making sure the maneuver is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On public roadways, bicycles are legally classified as:
options: a:Vehicles.,b:Objects.,c:Pedestrians.,d:Hazards.
note: Bicycles ridden on public roadways are treated as vehicles. Cyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles, including obeying traffic signals, signs, and lane markings, and yielding when required.

question: What does a curb painted red mean?
options: a:No stopping, standing, or parking at any time.,b:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:Loading zone.
note: A red curb means no stopping, standing, or parking at any time, except when required to obey a traffic control device or officer. You may not use a red curb area for loading, unloading, or waiting for passengers.

question: After which activity is reaction time slower?
options: a:Sleeping.,b:Working hard.,c:Drinking alcohol.
note: Alcohol slows your brain’s processing and muscle coordination, so your reaction time becomes longer. This makes it harder to notice hazards and respond in time, which is why driving after drinking is so dangerous.

question: If a tire blows out, which is the proper procedure?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it firmly.,b:Pull over quickly without slowing down.,c:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
note: When a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly to keep control, ease off the gas, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Once the vehicle is under control and slowing, apply the brakes lightly if needed and move to a safe place off the road.

question: If your wheels drop off the paved roadway onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce speed and re-enter the roadway gradually when it is safe.,b:Speed up and re-enter quickly.,c:Turn sharply back onto the roadway immediately.,d:Stop immediately where you are.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, keep steering straight, and gradually reduce speed while still on the shoulder. After you’ve slowed and checked for traffic, gently steer back onto the roadway; do not jerk the wheel or try to re-enter at high speed.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Try to fight it.,b:Take some caffeine pills.,c:Take a break.
note: Drowsy driving is very dangerous because your attention and reaction time are reduced and you may even fall asleep. If you feel drowsy, the safe choice is to pull over at a safe place, take a break, or switch drivers; do not try to fight sleep with tricks or caffeine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway, what is the proper action?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder to give them more room.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,d:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, you must be prepared to stop. Slow down, pass at a safe distance, and be ready to yield the right-of-way if they enter your path. Never speed up, crowd them, or drive on the shoulder to get around them.

question: How should you respond when confronted by an aggressive driver?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up to escape them.
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and move out of their way when it is safe. Do not race, block, or confront them, as this can escalate the situation and increase the risk of a collision.

question: Which behavior may indicate someone is driving aggressively?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Their tendency to drive slowly.,c:The number of passengers in their car.
note: Aggressive drivers often show risky behaviors such as tailgating, speeding, and making erratic or improper lane changes. If you see this, give them space, do not challenge them, and focus on keeping a safe distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing on the left, when may you safely move back into the right lane?
options: a:When the passed driver waves you back.,b:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are directly alongside the passed vehicle.,d:After three seconds have elapsed.
note: After passing another vehicle, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and have created a safe following distance. This ensures you do not cut them off and allows both drivers enough space to react.

question: If you are near a large commercial vehicle you should:
options: a:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,b:Signal aggressively to get ahead.,c:Follow closely to reduce wind drag.,d:Drive on its right side on curves and hills.
note: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots along both sides, especially on the right. Avoid driving beside them for long periods, and pass promptly and safely so the truck driver can see you and has room to maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection you should look:
options: a:Only to the right.,b:Left, right, then left again.,c:Only to the left.,d:Down the road only.
note: Before entering an intersection, scan in all directions: look left first (where the most immediate cross‑traffic comes from), then right, and left again. This helps you spot vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians that may be entering the intersection and ensures it is safe to proceed.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the roadway, even if there is no marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,b:Drive around them on the right if there is room.,c:Flash your headlights and proceed.,d:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are within a crosswalk and wait until the crosswalk is clear before proceeding.

question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.,b:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,c:When you are being tailgated by another driver.
note: If another driver is following too closely (tailgating), you should increase your following distance from the vehicle ahead. Extra space in front gives you more time to brake gradually and reduces the chance of being hit from behind if you must slow or stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Proceed with caution without stopping.,b:The light will soon turn green.,c:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop.,d:The same as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe and after yielding the right‑of‑way as required.

question: Which statement about driving and taking medications is true?
options: a:Prescription medicines never impair driving.,b:Many over-the-counter cold medicines can make you drowsy.,c:Medications are safe to use while driving if taken with coffee.,d:All over-the-counter medications are safe for driving.
note: Many over‑the‑counter medicines, especially cold and allergy medications, can cause drowsiness or slow your reactions, making driving unsafe. Always read labels and follow medical advice before driving after taking any medication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:During rush hour traffic.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: You must never enter an intersection unless you are sure you can clear it completely without stopping, regardless of the signal color. Even with a green light, if traffic ahead is stopped and you would be left blocking the cross street when the light changes, you must wait behind the stop line until there is enough space to fully clear the intersection.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Traffic next to the broken line may pass,b:The lane next to the solid line may pass anytime.,c:Neither lane may pass.,d:Both lanes may pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic traveling next to the broken line, and only when it is safe. Traffic next to the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass. This marking is used where passing is safe in one direction but not the other.

question: If you hit a parked car and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Wait for the owner to return.,b:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.,c:Call your insurance company when you get home.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you are legally required to leave a note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle. The note should include your name, contact information, and a brief description of the collision. You must also report the collision to law enforcement if damage meets your state’s reporting threshold.

question: Which statement about roadwork zones is correct?
options: a:Fines are always the same as in normal traffic.,b:Only slow down if workers are present.,c:You must slow down in work zones (Slow for the Cone Zone).,d:You may pass workers closely if traffic is light.
note: Work zones require you to slow down and drive with extra caution, even if you do not immediately see workers. Speeds are often reduced and fines are frequently higher in these areas to protect road workers and drivers. Always obey posted work-zone signs and be prepared for sudden stops, lane shifts, and equipment entering the roadway.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Motorcycles have no blind spots.,b:You can always see blind spots in your rearview mirrors.,c:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side.,d:Large trucks have larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: All vehicles have blind spots—areas you cannot see in your mirrors—and large trucks have much bigger blind spots than passenger cars. These areas are along both sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the truck. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, the driver likely cannot see you, so avoid lingering in these zones.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving you should:
options: a:Brake hard immediately to stop quickly.,b:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,c:Grip the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually before pulling off the road when safe.,d:Turn sharply off the road.
note: If a tire blows out or goes flat while driving, hold the steering wheel firmly to keep control, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, then move off the road to a safe place when you have the vehicle under control.

question: At a railroad crossing you must:
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all crossings and for multiple trains.,b:Ignore crossings if you do not see flashing lights.,c:Always cross immediately without stopping.,d:Assume only one train can approach at a time.
note: At railroad crossings, you must approach with caution, watch for vehicles such as school buses and tank trucks that are required to stop at all crossings, and look and listen for more than one train. Never assume the tracks are clear just because warning lights are off or one train has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To view objects in a blind spot when changing lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Only check the left outside mirror.,b:Only check the inside rearview mirror.,c:Look over your left or right shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, known as blind spots. Before changing lanes, quickly look over your left or right shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure no vehicle, motorcycle, bicycle, or pedestrian is in your blind spot.

question: When changing lanes, you should do which of the following?
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Change lanes without looking if you have signaled.,c:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,d:Rely only on the side mirror on the direction you're moving toward.
note: When changing lanes, first signal, then check your mirrors, and always glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on mirrors or signals; a quick shoulder check helps you see vehicles that may be hidden from your mirrors.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your headlights at them.,b:Slow down slightly but keep moving.,c:Speed up to pass before they run out.,d:Sound a sharp blast of your horn and be prepared to stop.
note: If a child is about to run into the street, you should immediately sound a sharp blast of your horn to warn them and other road users, and be ready to brake hard and stop. Children can act unpredictably, so reduce speed and be prepared to stop completely to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Follow the officer's directions and go through the intersection.,c:Stop until the light turns green.
note: Police officers directing traffic have authority over traffic signals and signs. If an officer clearly directs you to proceed through a red light, you must follow the officer’s instructions, moving carefully and watching for other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on an interstate?
options: a:Signaling before lane changes.,b:Changing lanes without signaling.,c:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,d:If you miss an exit, go to the next exit and turn around safely.
note: On interstates, you should always signal before changing lanes, and slower traffic should keep right. Changing lanes without signaling is unsafe and often illegal because other drivers cannot anticipate your movement. If you miss an exit, continue to the next one; never stop or back up on the interstate.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another vehicle is in your way.,c:When another driver makes a mistake.
note: Use your horn only when it may help prevent a collision, such as when another driver does not see you or is about to move into your lane. Do not use the horn to show anger, to urge others to drive faster, or simply because someone inconveniences you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection indicates you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Treat it as a green light.,c:Come to a complete stop.,d:Turn on your hazard lights.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed through the intersection only when it is safe. It does not give you the same right-of-way as a solid green light, and you are not required to stop unless needed for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct method to enter an expressway from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Go down the ramp and cross over to your desired traffic lane as soon as possible.,b:Use the acceleration lane to blend into traffic.,c:Go down to the bottom of the ramp and come to a complete stop before entering the expressway.
note: When entering an expressway, use the entrance and acceleration lane to build up speed to match the flow of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge when there is a safe gap. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless traffic or signals require it, because stopping makes merging dangerous.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road (hydroplaning), gently ease off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight. Do not brake or turn suddenly, because that can cause a skid. As your tires regain traction, you can gradually resume normal driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Allowed only from your direction of travel.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you may not use them to pass another moving vehicle.

question: When a school bus is loading or unloading children, what must you do?
options: a:Stop when the bus has flashing red lights and stop arm extended (with limited exceptions on divided highways).,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Stop only if you are driving in the same direction on any type of road.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. On a divided highway with a physical barrier or unpaved median, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop; on undivided roads, traffic in both directions must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.,b:When you are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:When you are on a hill or curve.
note: A broken line next to your lane means you may pass or change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so. A solid line next to your lane means you should not cross it to pass, and you must never attempt to pass on hills, curves, or anywhere you cannot see far enough ahead.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while driving primarily helps to:
options: a:Find police officers more easily.,b:Maintain a constant speed regardless of conditions.,c:Make lane changes automatically.,d:Reduce the need for last-second braking or turning.
note: Looking far ahead lets you spot problems early, such as slowing traffic or hazards in the road. By seeing these situations in advance, you can adjust your speed or lane smoothly and avoid sudden, last‑second braking or swerving.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.,c:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.
note: Orange construction signs and cones indicate a work zone. You must slow down as needed, be prepared to stop, and watch for workers, equipment, lane shifts, and reduced speed limits. Never assume you can maintain your normal speed through a work area.

question: A five-sided (pentagon) roadway sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A regulatory sign only.,b:A railroad crossing.,c:A school zone or school crossing.,d:A stop sign.
note: A five-sided (pentagon) sign is reserved for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

question: How should you drive in work zones regarding spacing?
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: In work zones you should increase your following distance and avoid tailgating. Extra space gives you more time to react to sudden stops, lane shifts, or workers and equipment entering the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the interstate, you should:
options: a:Expect other drivers to always let you in.,b:Check for a gap and merge when it is safe.,c:Merge across two lanes at once to find the fastest route.,d:Always stop at the end of the ramp before entering.
